messages:
alex: Quick question — our internal SDKs are returning 401 when Authorization is missing, but some prod clients report 403 when they only send X-Project-Id. Which should we standardize on?

maya: We decided on this a while back: 401 = missing/invalid credentials, 403 = authenticated but not authorized for the project/org.

sam: That matches my memory too, but the middleware has a fallback path: if Authorization is missing and X-Org-Id is present we try org-level lookup and might return 403. That could explain the confusion.

alex: Got it. Example causing confusion: client sends only X-Project-Id header (no Authorization) and gets 403. I would have expected 401.

maya: Right — the code does this: check credential -> if absent, then if X-Project-Id present try project->if project has a service token mapping we treat as implicit auth (then validate) else we return 401. But there's an older path where we check org fallback before returning 401.

kevin: TL;DR we should: 1) always return 401 if no credential header present (Authorization or x-api-key) regardless of X-Project-Id; 2) if credential present but not allowed for project return 403. That keeps contract stable for clients.

alex: I like that. Backcompat: some customers rely on the old behaviour (org fallback). Are we comfortable breaking that?

maya: We can preserve fallback behind a feature flag + opt-in for a short window. But the public API contract should be 401-vs-403 as kevin described.

sam: Also need to update SDKs — currently SDKs treat missing Authorization as 403 in 2 places. I'll open PRs.

alex: Can we also add an explicit error shape so clients can distinguish? Proposal: always return {"error":{"type":"auth","code":"missing_credentials"}} for 401 and {"error":{"type":"auth","code":"project_forbidden"}} for 403.

maya: Yes please. Add tests that assert the body shape. Keep it stable across versions.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: rolled auth-middleware v2.1.3 -> staging at 2024-05-05T14:32:10Z

kevin: On rotation: do we keep old key accepted for a grace period? current contract says 5m. We should document it and maybe extend to 10m for large customers.

alex: Document it in /docs/auth#key-rotation and add a warning in change log. Also add an audit log entry that records which key was used.

sam: I'll add tests in auth-integration that cover: missing Authorization + X-Project-Id => 401 + missing_credentials; Authorization wrong scope => 403 + project_forbidden; old key accepted during rotation window.

kevin: tagging @kevin for PR review :point_up: — alex can you file the RFC so we have an official spec?

alex: Will do. I'll open RFC and PRs for middleware + client SDKs. Thanks y'all :thumbsup:

kevin: Thanks — please include example request/response in the RFC. Example: 
```
GET /v1/completions
Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-Project-Id: proj-123

-> 403
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": {"type":"auth","code":"project_forbidden","message":"Token does not have access to proj-123"}
}
```

maya: And add a clear note: missing Authorization => 401 and body code missing_credentials.

alex: Filed RFC: rfc/2024-05-auth-headers-project-fallbacks.md (will link in PR).
